summary.text: Summarises, in English and French, two United Kingdom general-practice studies of mumps: a retrospective review of 1961–1967 and a prospective study from 1969 to 1971. It reports an overall rate of 6.6 cases per 1,000 patients a year, peak incidence in 5–14-year-olds and equal sex distribution, with orchitis and encephalitis as the main complications. Complications were more frequent in people over 15 and in high-incidence years, and most encephalitis patients had no lasting effects.
